CALL AND NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING

To the Members of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates:

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a special meeting of the City Council and
the Chair has called a special meeting of the Finance Advisory Committee to be held jointly and
called to order in the Council Chambers of City Hall, located at 340 Palos Verdes Dr. West, Palos
Verdes Estates, CA at 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, July 24, 2018. The agenda for the special meeting
with the items of business to be transacted or discussed is set forth below.

Posted by the Office of the City Clerk on Friday, Jul 20, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

  Jul 24, 2018
  5:00 p.m.
  Council Chambers of City Hall
  340 Palos Verdes Dr. West
  Palos Verdes Estates

  AGENDA
  OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  AND A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE FINANCE ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  TO BE HELD JOINTLY
Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities
Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request
a disability-related modification or accommodation.

The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the City Council meetings;
however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make
a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes or as specified by the Mayor. Anyone wishing
to address the City Council is requested to fill out a speaker’s card that is available in the meeting
room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minutes
preparation.

The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the
order of items shown on the agenda. Note: Agenda topics may be continued to future City Council
meetings.

   MEMORANDUM

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

SUBJECT: DISCUSSION AND CONSIDERATION OF FINANCE ADVISORY
  COMMITTEE WORKPLAN AND RESOURCES TO ACHIEVE THE GOALS
  FOR THE FINANCE ADVISORY COMMITTEE

DATE:  JULY 24, 2018

ISSUE

The purpose of this workshop is for the City Council and Finance Advisory to discuss the work plan
developed and proposed by the Finance Advisory Committee, and for the City Council to provide
direction and guidance to the Finance Advisory Committee.

BACKGROUND

In January 2018, the City Council established the Finance Advisory Committee (Committee).

In establishing the Committee, the general objective was to build within the community: trust,
transparency, knowledge, and communication about the City’s fiscal position and financial future.
Specifically, the Committee was established to advise and provide recommendations for maintaining
the City’s fiscal stability, communicating the City’s fiscal position, and achieving a long-range plan
for the City’s fiscal sustainability. As such, the ordinance establishing the Committee states that the
purpose of the Committee is:

1. To provide input and recommendations to the city council regarding budget reconciliation,
  including actual revenues and expenses at the departmental level;

2. To consult and work with staff in the preparation of long-range financial planning forecasts;

3. To advise and assist the city council on fiscal liability matters facing the city and other fiscal
  matters referred to the finance advisory committee.

In late January, the City Council appointed residents with diverse backgrounds, experiences and
interests to serve on the Committee for either a one-year or two-year term. Committee meetings

  Page 1 of 5

  001
 commenced in March 2018. When establishing the Committee, the City Council specified that the
Committee was to meet quarterly; however, the Committee commenced monthly meetings through
June primarily to formulate its work plan. Within this time period, the Committee additionally
participated in the City Council meetings pertaining to establishing the fiscal year 2018-2020 budget.

The Committee has establish five Ad Hoc Committees (Attachment A) to achieve its work plan
objectives. Through the Ad Hoc Committee process, the Committee initially intends to complete an
analysis of the fiscal year 2018-2019 operating and capital improvement budget. It is the
Committee’s goal by January 2019, to provide the City Council with general and specific
recommendations related to the validity, soundness, accounting, accuracy, justification, saving
opportunities, presentation, explanation, risks and vulnerabilities, and messaging of the budget.
Upon completing the evaluation, and based on the City Council’s subsequent direction, the
Committee, through the Ad Hoc Committees, intends to begin developing its long-range forecast.

DISCUSSION

The Finance Advisory Committee (Committee) has established the attached work plan (Attachment
B). The City Council is requested to review the work plan in reference to its goals and objectives
for the Committee and the resources that the City has available to support the Committee’s work.
Accordingly, and if necessary, the scope of the Committee as established by Ordinance can/will be
modified.

Staff has given much thought to the options, strategies and needed resources for supporting and
achieving the goals of the Committee. City staff are necessary to provide the research, analysis and
reports necessary for the Committee to achieve its objectives. Volunteers doing professional staff
work is not a practical or feasible solution; volunteers are not accountable for their work product in
the same manner as an employee, must be trained, necessitate supervision to verify the accuracy of
the report, require predictability in schedules to be effective working with staff, and in some
instances duplicate the work of staff. Volunteers with professional backgrounds, on the other hand,
may provide valuable advice and peer review of professional staff work.

Staff can accomplish the stated and presumed deliverables that have been discussed by the
Committee:

  •  Focusing on advising the City Council on financial policy, developing a long-range financial
  plan, identifying strategies for maintaining the City’s financial viability, proposing strategies
  for reducing liabilities, and formulating the messaging for City’s fiscal matters. This focus
  does not presume or entail the Committee conducting an assessment of City services, service
  levels, staffing and personnel related matters, or the justification of operations approved in
  the adopted budget.
  •  Meeting on a quarterly basis, providing staff in the intervening months with the time to
  develop and prepare the necessary work products.
  •  Receiving and responding to the work products and existing data provided by staff.

  Page 2 of 5

  002
   •  Working on a schedule to complete its recommendations for policy, communications, long-
  range financial planning forecasts, and fiscal liability matters by January 2020 1.
  •  Convening and working as a whole for all business, not as individual Ad Hoc Committees,
  for transparency, receiving the input from and working with a consensus of all Committee
  members, and managing staff time.
  •  Focusing its efforts on projects commensurate with the time available by existing staff and
  consultants.

  The fiscal year 2018-2019 budget includes a part-time Budget Analyst (Administrative Analyst) to
  assist in the implementation of several tasks and goals identified by the City Council and Committee.
  The City is also relying on interns for the launch of the enhanced OpenGov platform. The following,

  detail in operating budget and the organizational/service level functions of the City, the necessary

  staff time involved for the Committee’s line-item review would be longer.

  The Finance Department consists of 4 staff (Director, Senior Accountant, and two Finance Service
  Technicians) plus one part-time Budget Analyst for fiscal year 2018-2019. The Department with
  the existing staff level is at full capacity to achieve current work priorities in a timely manner.
  Expediting the deliverables that have been identified as a desirable for the community and / or adding
  additional tasks will require enhanced resources.

  CalPERS Pension Obligations

  Please recall that a CalPERS representative presented an explanation of the CalPERS pension
  program at the May 30, 2018 City Council and Finance Advisory Committee workshop/study
  session. At the meeting, the City Council directed staff to work with CalPERS to obtain a “fresh
  start” projection for options to pay down the City’s unfunded accrued liability (UAL) for pensions.
  Over the ensuing months, concurrent with two conference calls with CalPERS, the City has received
  the attached two spreadsheets (Attachment C). One spreadsheet is for Safety (sworn police) UAL
  and one spreadsheet is for Miscellaneous (non-sworn employees) UAL.

  Page 4 of 5

  004
 In the spreadsheets, there are 5 scenarios for paying down the UALs and the current 30-year plan (in
black). The green scenario is paying an additional hypothetical $500,000 above the payment for the
30-year plan. The red scenario is the 15-year plan either paid at a level % or a level $. The blue
scenario is the 20-year plan either paid at a level % or a level $. Please remember that the UAL is in
addition to the normal, regular payments made annually; for FY 2018-2019, this is $822,000. For
the work plan and goals of the Finance Advisory Committee, staff recommends that Committee
assess future costs and liabilities to determine

(1)  If a green, blue or red option should be pursued,

(2)  If the CalPERS’ interest rate is greater than the return on the City’s investments, whether or
  not to utilize some Reserve funds or other Fund resources to pay down the UAL, and / or

(3)  A policy recommendation for the use of one-time money or undesignated General Fund
  Balance for advancing payments.

CONCLUSION

It is absolute that the City will benefit from the advice and recommendations of the Finance Advisory
Committee (Committee). The Committee has an important purpose and value in adding validity and
credibility to the City’s presentation of our fiscal position, and in recommending a course for
sustaining the City’s fiscal vitality. The Committee will also be essential to effectively communicate
the City’s financial story.

Community engagement in the assessment and improvement of City finances is successfully
achieved through public input and assessment of data. The Committee is a key strategy to
accomplish this. In support of the Committee, staff must be trusted and relied upon for producing
reports, making recommendations, and implementing the City Council’s policy directives and
decisions. Mindful of the City’s existing resources (staff and funds), the deliverables that staff can
achieve to meet the goals of the City Council for the Committee are presented in this memorandum.
With increased resources, also identified in this report, are additional deliverables that can be
provided. Key to the timetable are several foundational assumptions as noted herein. It is requested
that based on the information herein, the expectations of the Committee and staff be discussed in the
context of the Committee’s work plan. As such, we will successfully fulfill and achieve the goals
of the City Council and Committee.

 APPEALS FOR VALUE REDUCTIONS
   THE ASSESSMENT APPEALS PROCESS
  An owner disagrees with the value enrolled by the assessor and files
  an appeal.

  An Administrative conference between the property owner and assessor’s staff
  is held.
  IF THERE IS AGREEMENT, THE VALUE IS CHANGED.

  IF AN AGREEMENT IS NOT REACHED, THE CASE MOVES TO THE AAB
FOR HEARING.
  THE CASE MUST  THE HEARING DECISION IS FINAL…
  BE HEARD WITHIN 2 YEARS  There is no appeal of the appeal.
   THE ASSESSMENT APPEALS PROCESS
IMPORTANT THINGS TO REMEMBER:

 The case is between the applicant and Appeals Board. A City does not have
  an opportunity to speak to the case unless they are subpoenaed by the
  Assessor staff to relate pertinent information.

 Appeals granted can be for multiple years.

 Tax payer refunds may be for multiple years and hit a single year’s property
  tax allocation. Refunds to the taxpayers are pooled using the AB8
  apportionment factors.

   THINGS TO REMEMBER WHEN BUDGETING
  PROPERTY TAX REVENUE
• The CPI for the 2018-19 Fiscal Year will be 2.00%

• Given the number of Proposition 8 restorations processed for 2017-18 there
  is about 24.6% of the pool of values left to be restored. The City should not
  count on a boost of more than 0.2% – 0.25% on restored value.

• In order for cities to see property value increases due to the new construction
  or sales activity, it needs to be completed and enrolled in December before
  the January lien date. For 2018-19 property taxes, that means the event had
  to be recorded by December 2017.
